tier_reason: Tier unchanged (C), now a flagged not-faster entry. Enricher e126 (2026-10-05): the chart win is 4 OpenMP threads against OpenCV's 32F GaussianBlur, whose current 4.x non-IPP path is sepFilter2D without parallel_for_ (author's OpenCV version unstated), so threads are unequal; the independent issue #3 (Ryzen 7 5800H, OpenCV 4.8, 720x720) measured OpenCV at 0.23 ms against the project's best stage at 0.63 ms, about 2.7x in OpenCV's favour. The SIMD and OpenMP loops also lack a tail guard and overrun a stack buffer when the width is not a multiple of 4 (the benchmarked widths are fine).

corrections.claimed_speedup: Not faster on a desktop CPU. First-party chart (Comparison.jpg, values read off bars): final stage (memory management + SIMD + OpenMP, 4 threads) about 3.4 ms vs OpenCV about 8.9 ms at 720x720, 7.9 vs 19.8 ms at 1080x1080, 13.7 vs 35 ms at 1440x1440, roughly 2.5x (derived from page data) on a Raspberry Pi 3B+; the project's own single-thread stages are slower than OpenCV at every size (about 10.0-11.6 vs 8.9 ms at 720x720). Independent (issue #3, Ryzen 7 5800H, OpenCV 4.8, 720x720): OpenCV 0.23 ms vs the project's best stage 0.63 ms, OpenCV about 2.7x faster (derived from page data).
corrections.caveats: Tutorial rather than a library (About: 'Step-by-step tutorial for optimizing a Gaussian image smoothing function'). The win comes only from the OpenMP stage spreading rows across the Pi's four cores against a single-threaded OpenCV path (the current 4.x non-IPP GaussianBlur 32F path is sepFilter2D without parallel_for_; the author's OpenCV version, build options and thread count are not stated); the project's own single-thread SIMD stage is slower than OpenCV at all three sizes, and the independent issue #3 run on a Ryzen 7 5800H with OpenCV 4.8 has OpenCV 2.7x faster. The harness never checks the output against OpenCV's. CMakeLists sets -O3 -Ofast -funroll-loops (-fopenmp for the parallel stage) but no -mfpu=neon on a 32-bit OS, so NEON use is unproven. Bugs: the SIMD and OpenMP loops lack a tail guard and overrun a stack buffer when the width is not divisible by 4; the top-row 'leftovers' loop redeclares j and recomputes the whole row in scalar. Kernel weights are hard-coded for sigma 1.0 and a 5x5 kernel. Uses operators removed in OpenCV 4.11, so it will not compile against current OpenCV (issue #2: compile error on OpenCV 3.3). No license file, so reference only. Last commit 2021-03-25.
